bs-init-project: berkispec - 00. Use it at the very first start of the project (Phase 00), or if the root 'conventions.md' is missing/incomplete. Together with the developer it records the global project conventions (tech stack, tests, development flow, git merge strategy) in 'conventions.md' — this is the prerequisite of every further phase.
bs-add-cycles: berkispec - 01. Use it after initialization (Phase 01) to plan development cycles (roadmap), to reschedule existing ones or to add a new cycle — splitting the work into logical, independently testable units. Input: 'conventions.md', optionally a brainstorm session ('brainstorm: NN' — it distils 'cycle-design-input.md' from the working file of '/bs-brainstorm', BS18). It creates or updates 'specs/roadmap.md' with 'Done' status.
bs-write-spec: berkispec - 02. Use it when starting a cycle (Phase 02) based on the roadmap, to specify the functional/business requirements. It works on the git branch of the cycle (the branch was created in phase 01 from 'main'), and creates 'spec.md' ('Ready for planning') + 'spec-questions.md'. Prerequisite: 'specs/roadmap.md' status 'Done'.
bs-write-code-plan: berkispec - 03a. Use it when the spec.md of the cycle is 'Ready for planning' (Phase 03a), to work out the code side of the technical implementation plan: environment coordinates, planned changes (with a purpose), configuration, schema artifacts, the scope gate (code base analysis, the researcher subagent if needed). It closes plan.md with the 'Ready for test planning' status; the test plan is written by /bs-write-test-plan.
bs-write-test-plan: berkispec - 03b. Use it when the plan.md of the cycle is 'Ready for test planning' (Phase 03b), to work out the test plan: TS-NN test scenarios with a step table and an .http form, the machine-readable run table, environment preparation, test artifact data sheets, spec coverage, regression. It closes plan.md with the 'Ready for tasks' status.
bs-write-tasks: berkispec - 04. Use it when plan.md is 'Ready for tasks' (Phase 04), to split the technical plan into well-structured, individually executable and measurable items (DoD). It creates 'tasks.md' ('Ready for implementation') + 'tasks-questions.md' if needed.
bs-analyze: berkispec - 05. Use it before the implementation (Phase 05), when tasks.md is 'Ready for implementation'. A cross-phase consistency gate between spec.md/plan.md/tasks.md: with subagents (analyzer, *-fixer) it identifies and automatically fixes the contradictions. It creates 'analyze-report.md' (PASS/FAIL).
bs-implement: berkispec - 06. Use it when analyze-report.md is 'PASS' (Phase 06), for the actual code development. It carries out the planned code changes based on the task list, and maintains 'tasks.md' along the way until it reaches the 'Ready for validation' state.
bs-validate: berkispec - 07. Use it after the implementation (Phase 07), when tasks.md is 'Ready for validation'. Test, lint and build verification AND code review in a single self-healing loop (test-runner, reviewer, implement-fixer, review-fixer subagents). It creates 'validation-report.md' and 'code-review.md'; on PASS it sets the status of spec.md/plan.md/tasks.md to 'Done'.
bs-doc-sync: berkispec - 08. Use it after validation, before the merge (Phase 08), when tasks.md/plan.md/spec.md are all 'Done'. It synchronizes the code changes into the 'docs-generated/' system documentation and into the affected component READMEs (doc-sync-planner subagent, against design drift), maintains the 'specs/test-conventions.md' register of recurring test expectations, and creates 'doc-sync-plan.md'.
bs-review-and-merge: berkispec - 09. Use it as the last step of the cycle (Phase 09) if every document is 'Done' AND the '## Review and merge' section of conventions.md says 'PR submission: no'. A single skill: bringing the main branch into the cycle branch → post-merge test round (VP2: tests + Sonar) → merge with mandatory user confirmation (RD8) → closing the roadmap. With a PR requirement it errors out and redirects to the bs-create-pr → bs-review → bs-merge chain.
bs-create-pr: berkispec - 09a. Use it as the first step of the end of the cycle (Phase 09a) if the '## Review and merge' section of conventions.md says 'PR submission: yes'. Pushing the cycle branch and opening the PR according to the Merge strategy of conventions.md — it does NOT merge the PR; the review and the merge are the job of bs-review and bs-merge.
bs-review: berkispec - 09b. Use it after the PR has been opened (Phase 09b). It runs the reviewer subagent on the diff of the PR — in centralized SDD as a machine run on the CI/CD — and writes into 'test-report/ci-code-review.md'; it never overwrites the local 'code-review.md' of 07. On an open Must Fix it notifies and leaves the PR open.
bs-merge: berkispec - 09c. Use it after the review that ran on the PR (Phase 09c). It checks the state of the PR (is it approved — this takes over the role of RD8) and both review reports, runs the post-merge test round (VP2: tests + Sonar) on the cycle branch, and gets the code onto the main branch ONLY after a green result.
bs-dev-test: berkispec - 09d. An OPTIONAL last phase (Phase 09d), only in centralized SDD, if conventions.md says 'Dev deployment test: yes'. After a successful merge it deploys the product into a fully integrated test environment, runs real e2e tests against it (VP3), puts the evidence into the 'test-report/dev-test/' folder of the cycle, and — if that is the last enabled verification — closes the cycle.
bs-brainstorm: berkispec - helper command. Exploratory ideation and joint design about the project BEFORE THE SPEC — when the direction of the topic, the way to implement it or its split into cycles is not clear yet (e.g. 'how should central cert management work?'). It converses, contrasts alternatives, and persists the material of the session into the '.bs-brainstorm/brainstorm-NN-<slug>.md' working file. It writes no code and NOTHING outside the working file; at the end it hands over to the '/bs-add-cycles' or the '/bs-quick-flow' skill.
bs-cycle-status: berkispec - helper command. Checking the status of the cycles. It lists the cycles of the project (Done/In progress), and shows the progress of their phases in detail on an interactive TUI or when given as an argument (DONE, DONE*, IN PROGRESS, NOT RUN YET). It is not a phase: it is not part of the 00-09 process, it can be called at any time.
bs-export-doc: berkispec - helper command. It produces a versioned PDF from markdown documents (together with the mermaid diagrams) into the 'export/' folder in the root of the project. Without a parameter from the 'docs-generated/architecture.md' and 'system-overview.md' files, otherwise from the named file(s). The version number is independent per file: the last one + 1, starting from v1.
bs-quick-flow: berkispec - quick-flow. A simplified, three-phase SDD flow (spec-plan.md → tasks.md → implementation) for SMALL, well-bounded tasks that can be solved in 3-4 steps — configuration, a simpler script, a smaller fix, a local modification. Do NOT use it for a task that requires substantial coding, a feature touching several components or complex design — recommend the full berki spec process instead (01-add-cycles).
bs-manual-test-plan: berkispec - helper command. Assembling the manual test plan of the cycle: component startup, test data, manual call sequences (curl + .http), expected results, and the place of the results of the automated tests. It works in two modes: 'Planned' (before the implementation, based on plan.md) or 'As-built' (after the validation, checked against the code). Prerequisite: the status of analyze-report.md is 'PASS'. Not a phase: it is not part of the 00-09 process, it does not change any cycle status, it can be called any time after the analyze and re-run any time (it keeps the manual additions).
bs-run-tests: berkispec - helper command. Running tests outside a cycle, per category: it runs run-tests.py from the project-level run table of the 'Test execution' section of conventions.md, and writes the result into the gitignored 'test-runs/<category>/<UTC-timestamp>/<env>/' tree, with a per-category 'latest.json' pointer. Its input is the 'Test execution' section of conventions.md (written by 00-init-project together with the user); cycle-level execution still goes through the machine-readable table of plan.md. Not a phase: it is not part of the 00-09 process, it does not change a cycle status, it can be re-run any time — and its result is NEVER cycle evidence: the validation gates of 07 reject a path under test-runs/.

analyzer-exec.description: Read-only EXECUTABILITY diagnosis of the plan.md/tasks.md pair before the implementation (the judgement-heavy checks of category 6: a test promised in prose, artifact ownership, the completeness of a destructive operation, anchor symbols, artifact voice). The 05-analyze skill calls it, IN PARALLEL with the `analyzer`.
analyzer-exec.role: Executability and artifact-ownership analyst specialist agent

analyzer.description: Read-only cross-phase SEMANTIC consistency diagnosis across spec.md/plan.md/tasks.md/conventions.md, before implementation (categories 1–5: duplication, ambiguity, under-specification, convention conflict, coverage interpretation). The caller gives a SCOPE (s1-dup-underspec / s2-coverage / s3-conventions), so it runs in three parallel rounds, each from the slice cut by the gate. Category 6 is carried by analyzer-exec, also in parallel. Invoked by the 05-analyze skill.

doc-sync-planner.description: A read-only diagnostician that produces the per-file checkable plan of updating docs-generated/ and the finished replacement texts (doc-sync-plan.md). The 08-doc-sync skill calls it.

implement-fixer.description: The fixing entry point of the 07-validate self-healing loop: it delegates to the Fix mode of 06-implement to fix the test/Sonar/DoD failures (## Validation fixes). The 07-validate skill calls it.
implement-fixer.role: Implement Fix-mode executor wrapper (the 06-phase fixer of the validate loop)

plan-fixer.description: The 03-plan Fix-mode entry point of the 05-analyze self-healing loop (a thin wrapper around the Fix mode of 03a-write-code-plan / 03b-write-test-plan — it may correct both halves of plan.md). The 05-analyze skill calls it.
plan-fixer.role: Plan Fix-mode executor wrapper (the 03-phase fixer of the analyze loop)

researcher.description: A read-only code base and documentation researcher that returns a concise path+summary list (context saving, not raw file content) — except when the caller explicitly asks for literal values (command, URL, JSON payload, signature), which it returns verbatim. Phases 00/01/02/03/06 and the bs-brainstorm helper command call it for exploration.
researcher.role: Code base and documentation researcher specialist agent (context guard)

review-fixer.description: The fixing entry point of the review branch of 07-validate: it delegates to the Fix mode of 06-implement based on ## Review fixes. The 07-validate skill calls it.
review-fixer.role: Review Fix-mode executor wrapper (the review branch of the self-healing loop of 07)

reviewer.description: A read-only code review diagnostician: it examines the diff of the cycle branch and produces test-report/code-review.md (Must Fix / Suggestion). The 07-validate skill calls it, as step 2 of the full round (the static layer, next to Sonar).

spec-fixer.description: The 02-spec Fix-mode entry point of the 05-analyze self-healing loop (a thin wrapper around the Fix mode of 02-write-spec). The 05-analyze skill calls it.
spec-fixer.role: Spec Fix-mode executor wrapper (the 02-phase fixer of the analyze loop)

tasks-fixer.description: The 04-tasks Fix-mode entry point of the 05-analyze self-healing loop (a thin wrapper around the Fix mode of 04-write-tasks). The 05-analyze skill calls it.
tasks-fixer.role: Tasks Fix-mode executor wrapper (the 04-phase fixer of the analyze loop)

test-runner.description: Mechanical execution and factual summary of tests/Sonar/E2E (it does not decide on PASS/FAIL). 07-validate — and indirectly the re-validate of 09 — calls it.
test-runner.role: Test and code-quality runner specialist agent (mechanical executor — it reports facts, it does not decide)
